title: Local truths, global maps
lede: Three honest maps of one road. Watch them glue into a single map, and watch one metre of disagreement refuse to.

audience.who: engineers and designers who have never opened a topology book
audience.leaves_knowing: local truths glue into a global one exactly when they agree on every overlap; the leftover when they do not has a name and a number

critique_of_obvious: The textbook picture is a blob with smaller blobs inside it and arrows labelled with Greek letters. It never shows a number disagreeing, so the viewer never feels why gluing can fail.
mechanism: A sheaf assigns to every patch of a space the data that is true there, together with restriction maps that shrink data from a patch to any smaller patch inside it. Two patches that overlap can be compared by restricting both to the overlap. If a family of local data agrees on every overlap, the sheaf axiom says it glues to one global datum, uniquely. When the patches wrap around a loop, the offsets on the overlaps can sum to something non-zero, and then no global datum exists: that sum is the first cohomology class, the leftover disagreement.

anchor.what: one loop road unrolled across the top, with three surveyors' map patches A, B, C laid over it and corners p, q, r marked

worked_example.derivation: On each overlap the offset is g_XY = X(corner) − Y(corner): g_AB at p, g_BC at q, g_CA at r. Around the loop the cocycle sum is g_AB + g_BC + g_CA. If it is 0, shifts s_A = 0, s_B = g_AB, s_C = g_AB + g_BC glue the readings into one elevation map (reading + shift = true elevation at every corner). Replace A(r) by the misread value and recompute: the sum is the leftover in metres, and no re-choice of shifts changes it because any coboundary sums to 0.
worked_example.abstraction_note: The elevation profile between corners is drawn as a smooth curve through the three true elevations; only the corner readings are data.

beats.label: One road, 3 maps
beats.caption: One road loops around a city. Three surveyors each map their own arc of it, and nobody maps the whole loop.
beats.idea: A space is covered by overlapping patches, each with its own local data.
beats.focal_motion: the road draws on left to right; patches A, B, C land over their arcs in turn

beats.label: Local truths
beats.caption: Each map is honest on its own arc: A reads corner p at 12 m, B reads the same corner at 15 m.
beats.idea: Local data can be true on its own patch and still differ from a neighbour's.
beats.focal_motion: each map's elevation profile draws on beneath its patch, at its own datum height

beats.label: Overlaps
beats.caption: Where two maps cover the same street they can be compared. That shared stretch is the overlap.
beats.idea: Only on an overlap can two patches be compared.
beats.focal_motion: the three overlap columns highlight in turn on the road and on the profile

beats.label: Restriction
beats.caption: Restrict both maps to the overlap and the disagreement is a constant: B sits exactly 3 m above A.
beats.idea: Restricting to an overlap exposes the offset between two patches.
beats.focal_motion: the readings table in the detail band resolves into three offsets, one per overlap

beats.label: Around the loop
beats.caption: Walk the offsets around the loop and add them up: −3, −2, +5. The total is zero.
beats.idea: The offsets around a loop sum to a single number.
beats.focal_motion: a vermillion thread travels the loop and the three offsets sum in the detail band

beats.label: Glue
beats.caption: Zero means the maps glue. Shift B down 3 and C down 5 and one elevation map covers the whole loop.
beats.idea: Agreement on every overlap yields one unique global datum.
beats.focal_motion: the B and C profile segments slide down onto A's datum and the three become one line

beats.label: The leftover
beats.caption: Misread one corner by a metre and the total is −1. No choice of datums removes it: that leftover is the obstruction.
beats.idea: A non-zero loop sum is an obstruction no re-choice of local data can remove.
beats.focal_motion: A's end at r lifts by 1 m; the loop no longer closes and a vermillion gap bracket marks the leftover

beats.label: Why it matters
beats.caption: An agent's retrieve, edit, test and commit are patches on one codebase. They glue, or the harness fails at the seam.
beats.idea: Agent steps are local sections; a harness is the gluing test.
beats.focal_motion: the glued profile re-lights and the three map labels take their agent-step names

aha: A sheaf is a rule for what counts as true on a patch, plus a promise: local truths that agree wherever they overlap glue into one global truth, uniquely. When they do not, the disagreement is not noise. It is a number with a name, and it tells you where the seam is. Agents, maps, and codebases all live under that rule.

refs.title: Mac Lane & Moerdijk, Sheaves in Geometry and Logic, ch. II (sheaves and the gluing axiom)
Bott & Tu, Differential Forms in Algebraic Topology, §10 (Čech cohomology of a good cover)
Batruin, Capability Sheaves for Compositional Agent-Harness Repair

claims.text: A section over a patch is data true on that patch, and restriction to any smaller patch is well defined.
Sections that agree on every pairwise overlap glue to a unique global section (the sheaf axiom).
For a three-patch cover of a circle with constant offsets, a global section exists iff the offsets sum to zero; the sum represents the class in H¹.
An agent's tool steps can be modelled as local sections over a shared codebase, with the harness checking whether they glue.
